gap: No result ChatGPT got states that named reviewers measured the 13.3-inch Mobile Pixels Duex Plus (the model before today's Duex Plus DS) at 152 nits (Parka Blogs, July 2022) and about 200 nits (MBReviews, January 2022) against the maker's 300-nit rating.
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages: The Dad Sneeze, iTechGuides '15 Best' and Wondrik. The Dad Sneeze lists the Duex Plus DS at 250 nits as a spec, already warns that this 'is dim next to most laptops', and says itself it is 'a researched roundup, not a hands-on test'. iTechGuides repeats Mobile Pixels' '300-nit, 60 Hz class' and credits no reviewer or lab. Wondrik does carry named measurements, but only for freestanding monitors, and gives the M14d only its 300-nit rating. So no cited page has a measured figure for any attached extender, but the takeaway ('dim') is already on the cited Dad Sneeze page. Both measurements are of the 2022 Duex Plus, not the current DS, and I could not open RTINGS' own figures (its pages returned only navigation).
decides: It does not change the pick; it qualifies it. The Duex Plus DS stays the attached pick for a 13-inch laptop on fit and video path, but the page should not repeat '300 nits' as fact: the only measurements I could open are of the older 13.3-inch Duex Plus and came in at half to two-thirds of the rating. Say plainly that no named measurement of the DS revision was found. For a shopper who works near a window, that gap supports a freestanding monitor instead. For the Trio 3 Pro, Macworld's review adds that its screens do not reach full brightness on laptop power alone and that it weighs 4.13 lb, which counts against it on a 13-inch laptop.
